sentence: Krishna notes that enemies will spread scandal and mock one's courage [2.36].
verse_text: And your enemies will speak many indecent words while denigrating your might. What can be more painful than that?

sentence: Arjuna admits that he once addressed Krishna with thoughtless familiarity, not understanding His true greatness [11.41].
verse_text: Without knowing this greatness of Yours, whatever was said by me (to You) rashly, through inadvertence or even out of intimacy, thinking (You to be) a friend, addressing (You) as 'O krsna,' 'O Yadava,' 'O friend,' etc.-.

sentence: Krishna says that harmlessness, truth, absence of anger, compassion towards all, and gentleness are qualities of a person [16.2].

sentence: Krishna explains that humility, harmlessness, and forgiveness are also important traits [13.8].
verse_text: Humility, unpretentiousness, non-injury, for-bearance, sincerity, service of the teacher, cleanliness, steadiness, control of body and organs;

sentence: Krishna states that one who does not harm the world and is not carried away by anger or fear is dear to Him [12.15].
verse_text: He, too, owing to whom the world is not disturbed, and who is not disturbed by the world, who is free from joy, impatience, fear and anxiety, is dear to Me.

sentence: Krishna notes that harmlessness and equanimity are qualities that arise from Him [10.5].
verse_text: Non-injury, eanimity, satisfaction, austerity, charity, fame, infamy-(these) different dispositions of beings spring from Me alone.

sentence: Krishna says that even the wise are confused about what constitutes action and inaction [4.16].
verse_text: Even the intelligent are confounded as to what is action and what is inaction. I shall tell you of that action by knowing which you will become free from evil.

sentence: Krishna explains that ancient seekers who wanted freedom performed their actions regardless of this confusion [4.15].
verse_text: Having known thus, duties were performed even by the ancient seekers of Liberation. Thererfore you undertake action itself as was performed earlier by the ancient ones.

sentence: Krishna suggests that one should attain peace little by little by using reason and fortitude [6.25].

sentence: Krishna states that peace follows when one renounces the fruits of their actions [12.12].

sentence: Krishna says that one should learn by prostrating, by questioning, and by serving, as the wise who have realized the truth will instruct one in that knowledge [4.34].
verse_text: Know that through prostration, iniry and service. The wise ones who have realized the Truth will impart the Knowledge to you.

sentence: Krishna explains that constant yearning for the knowledge of the Self and pondering over the lessons of the great truth is wisdom, while all else is ignorance [13.12].
verse_text: Steadfastness in the knowledge of the Self, contemplation on the Goal of the knowledge of Reality-this is spoken of as Knowledge. Ignorance is that which is other than this.

sentence: Krishna warns that the ignorant man, the one who has no faith, and the skeptic are lost, as there is no happiness for one who always doubts [4.40].
verse_text: One who is ignorant and faithless, and has a doubting mind perishes. Neither this world nor the next nor happiness exists for one who has a doubting mind.

sentence: Krishna states that when one's reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, one becomes indifferent to the philosophies already heard and those yet to be heard [2.52].
verse_text: When your mind will go beyond the turbidity of delusion, then you will acire dispassion for what has to be heard and what has been heard.

sentence: Krishna says that one should perform all actions with the mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye [2.48].
verse_text: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

sentence: Krishna explains that one should fix their mind on Him, devote themselves to Him, sacrifice for Him, and make Him the object of their aspirations [9.34].
verse_text: Having your mind fixed on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, and bow down to Me. By concentrating your mind and accepting Me as the supreme Goal, you shall surely attain Me who am thus the Self.

sentence: Krishna states that this inner severance from the affliction of misery should be practised with determination and with a heart that refuses to be depressed [6.23].
verse_text: One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga has to be practised with perservance and with an undepressed heart.

sentence: Krishna suggests that one should cling to right action, as spirituality is the real art of living [2.50].
verse_text: Possessed of wisdom, one rejects here both virtue and vice. Therefore devote yourself to (Karma-) yoga. Yoga is skilfulness in action.

sentence: Arjuna asks Krishna why he is being urged to engage in action if knowledge is considered superior [3.1].
verse_text: Arjuna said O Janardana (krsna), if it be Your opinion that wisdom is superior to action, why they do you urge me to horrible aciton, O Kesava ?

sentence: Krishna explains that it is better to perform one's own duty, even if it is done imperfectly, rather than to follow the duty of another [18.47].
verse_text: One's own duty, (though) defective, is superior to another's duty well performed. By performing a duty as dictated by one's own nature, one does not incur sin.

sentence: Krishna further suggests that if one cannot practice deep concentration, one may still attain perfection by performing all actions for His sake [12.10].
verse_text: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

sentence: Krishna states that by fixing the mind on Him, being devoted, and making Him the supreme goal, one becomes united with Him [9.34].
verse_text: Having your mind fixed on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, and bow down to Me. By concentrating your mind and accepting Me as the supreme Goal, you shall surely attain Me who am thus the Self.

sentence: Krishna says that even the wise are often confused about the true nature of action and inaction [4.16].

sentence: Krishna explains that it is necessary to consider what is right action, what is wrong action, and what is inaction, because the law of action is mysterious [4.17].
verse_text: For there is something to be known even about action, and something to be known about prohibited action; and something has to be known about inaction. The true nature of action is inscrutable.

sentence: Krishna states that the knowledge, the act, and the doer differ according to the qualities [18.19].
verse_text: Knowledge, action and agent are stated in the teaching about the gunas to be only of three kinds according to the differences of the gunas. Hear about them also as they are.

sentence: Krishna also says that physical action is far inferior to an intellect concentrated on the divine, and that it is only the petty-minded who work for reward [2.49].

sentence: Arjuna also tells Krishna that his apparently perplexing speech confuses his understanding and asks for one certain way to attain bliss [3.2].

verse_text: Actions do not taint Me; for Me there is no hankering for the results of actions. One who knows Me thus, does not become bound by actions.

sentence: Krishna says that attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses, and he advises that one should not come under their sway because they are foes [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: Krishna states that the enjoyments born of contacts are only generators of pain, as they have a beginning and an end, and the wise man does not rejoice in them [5.22].
verse_text: Since enjoyments that result from contact (with objects) are verily the sources of sorrow and have a beginning and an end, (therefore) O son of Kunti, the wise one does not delight in them.

sentence: Krishna explains that it is only the petty-minded who work for reward, and he suggests seeking refuge in wisdom [2.49].
verse_text: O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.

sentence: Krishna also says that one should perform their bounden duty, as action is superior to inaction [3.8].
verse_text: You perform the obligatory duties, for action is superior to inaction. And, through inaction, even the maintenance of your body will not be possible.

sentence: Krishna says that the Spirit is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, and the immutable, and knowing the Spirit as such, one has no cause to grieve [2.25].
verse_text: It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

sentence: Krishna explains that great souls who attain Him go no more to the misery and death of earthly life, for they have gained perfection [8.15].
verse_text: As a result of reaching Me, the exalted ones who have attained the highest perfection do not get rirth which is an abode of sorrows and which is impermanent.

sentence: Krishna also notes that after many lives, the wise man realizes Him as He is [7.19].
verse_text: At the end of many births the man of Knowledge attains Me, (realizing) that Vasudeva is all. Such a high-souled one is very rare.

sentence: Krishna says that death is certain for the born and birth is certain for the dead, so one should not grieve for what is inevitable [2.27].
verse_text: For death of anyone born is certain, and of the dead (re-) birth is a certainly. Therefore you ought not to grieve over an inevitable fact.

sentence: Krishna also states that the Self is unmanifested, unthinkable, and unchangeable, and knowing this, one has no cause to grieve [2.25].
verse_text: It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

sentence: Krishna explains that Yoga is the severance from union with pain, and this should be practiced with determination and an undesponding mind [6.23].
verse_text: One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga has to be practised with perservance and with an undepressed heart.

sentence: Krishna says that just as the soul experiences infancy, youth, and old age within one body, it eventually passes into another body, and the wise feel no delusion about this [2.13].
verse_text: As are boyhood, youth and decrepitude to an embodied being in this (present) body, similar is the acisition of another body. This being so, an intelligent person does not get deluded.

sentence: Krishna explains that the soul is never born and never dies, remaining eternal and changeless even when the physical body is destroyed [2.20].
verse_text: Never is this One born, and never does It die; nor is it that having come to exist, It will again cease to be. This One is birthless, eternal, undecaying, ancient; It is not killed when the body is killed.

sentence: Krishna also notes that beings are unmanifested before birth and after death, existing only in a manifested state during their middle life, which leaves no cause for grief [2.28].
verse_text: O descendant of Bharata, all beings remain unmanifest in the beginning;; they become manifest in the middle. After death they certainly become unmanifest. What lamentation can there be with regard to them?

sentence: Krishna says that one should restrain the senses and sit steadfast, as the wisdom of one who controls their senses is steady [2.61].
verse_text: Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.

sentence: Krishna explains that attachment and aversion for sense objects abide in the senses, and he advises that one should not come under their sway because they are foes [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: Krishna suggests that one should attain quietude little by little by holding the intellect firmly and fixing the mind on the Self [6.25].
verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: Krishna also notes that if one is unable to practice concentration, one can still attain the goal by doing all actions for his sake [12.10].
verse_text: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

sentence: Krishna says that one should perform their prescribed duty, as action is superior to inaction and the maintenance of the body would be impossible without it [3.8].
verse_text: You perform the obligatory duties, for action is superior to inaction. And, through inaction, even the maintenance of your body will not be possible.

sentence: Krishna suggests that if one is unable to practice concentration, they might devote themselves to service and perform all acts for His sake to attain the goal [12.10].
verse_text: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

sentence: Krishna advises that one should attain peace little by little by using reason controlled by fortitude, fixing the mind on the Self and thinking of nothing else [6.25].
verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: Krishna explains that one who restrains their senses and meditates steadfastly achieves perfection [2.61].
verse_text: Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.

sentence: Arjuna admits that the mind is fickle, turbulent, obstinate, and as difficult to control as the wind [6.34].
verse_text: For, O Krsna, the mind is unsteady, turbulent, strong and obstinate. I consider its control to be as greatly difficult as of the wind.

sentence: Krishna says that when the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away one's discrimination just as a ship is tossed by a tempest [2.67].
verse_text: For, the mind which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, that (mind) carries away his wisdom like the mind (diverting) a boat on the waters.

sentence: Krishna explains that when the wavering mind wanders, one should restrain it and bring it back under the control of the Self [6.26].
verse_text: (The yogi) should bring (this mind) under the subjugation of the Self Itself, by restraining it from all those causes whatever due to which the restless, unsteady mind wanders away.

sentence: Krishna suggests that one should gradually attain peace by holding the intellect firmly and fixing the mind on the Self [6.25].
verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: Arjuna admits that his heart is oppressed by pity and his mind is confused regarding his duty, so he asks for clear direction [2.7].
verse_text: With my nature overpowered by weak commiseration, with a mind bewildered about duty, I supplicate You. Telll me for certain that which is better; I am Your disciple. Instruct me who have taken refuge in You.

sentence: Krishna says that one has the right to work, but never to the fruits of that work, and one should not be motivated by those results [2.47].
verse_text: Your right is for action alone, never for the results. Do not become the agent of the results of action. May you not have any inclination for inaction.

sentence: Krishna explains that physical action is inferior to an intellect concentrated on the Divine, and those who work for rewards are petty-minded [2.49].
verse_text: O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.

sentence: Krishna also states that peace follows the renunciation of the fruits of actions [12.12].
verse_text: Knowledge is surely superior to practice; meditation surpasses knowledge. The renunciation of the results of works (excels) meditation. From renunciation, Peace follows immediately.

sentence: Krishna says that those who work for the sake of reward are considered petty-minded and should instead seek refuge in wisdom [2.49].
verse_text: O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.

sentence: Krishna explains that a person who abandons attachment to the fruits of their actions remains content and independent, even while they are engaged in activity [4.20].
verse_text: Having given up attachment to the results of action, he who is ever-contented, dependent on nothing, he really does not do anything even though engaged in action.

sentence: Krishna states that by keeping the mind balanced and controlled, one attains a peace that abides in Him [6.15].
verse_text: Concentrating the mind thus for ever, the yogi of controlled mind achieves the Peace which culminates in Liberation and which abides in Me.

sentence: Krishna says that he transcends both the perishable and the imperishable, being declared the highest Purusha in the world [15.18].
verse_text: Since I am transcendental to the mutable and above even the immutable, hence I am well known in the world and in the Vedas as the supreme Person.

sentence: Krishna explains that the one who sees him in everything and everything in him is never separated from him [6.30].
verse_text: One who sees Me in everything, and sees all things in Me-I do not out of his vision, and he also is not lost to My vision.

sentence: Krishna states that through devotion, one knows him in truth and enters the Supreme [18.55].
verse_text: Through devotion he knows Me in reality, as to what and who I am. Then, having known Me in truth, he enters (into Me) immediately after that (Knowledge).

sentence: Krishna describes the path of unswerving devotion as involving a love for solitude and indifference to social life [13.11].
verse_text: And unwavering devotion to Me with single-minded concentration; inclination to repair into a clean place; lack of delight in a crowd of people;

sentence: Krishna says that one should perform all actions with the mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye [2.48].
verse_text: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

sentence: Krishna suggests that by surrendering actions unto Him and concentrating the intellect on Him, one can think always of Him [18.57].
verse_text: Mentally surrendering all actions to Me and accepting Me as the supreme, have your mind ever fixed on Me by resorting to the concentration of your intellect.

sentence: Krishna explains that a person who keeps the mind balanced and controlled attains the peace that abides in Him [6.15].
verse_text: Concentrating the mind thus for ever, the yogi of controlled mind achieves the Peace which culminates in Liberation and which abides in Me.

sentence: Krishna advises that one should fight while free from selfishness, anticipation of reward, and mental excitement [3.30].
verse_text: Devoid of the fever of the soul, engage in battle by dedicating all actions to Me, with (your) mind intent on the Self, and becoming free from expectations and egoism.

sentence: Krishna says that one should raise oneself by one's own Self, as the Self is the only friend or enemy of oneself [6.5].
verse_text: One should save oneself by oneself; one should not lower oneself. For oneself is verily one's onw friend; oneself is verily one's own enemy.

sentence: Krishna explains that if one is unable to practice concentration, one may still attain perfection by performing all actions for His sake [12.10].
verse_text: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

sentence: Krishna also notes that austerity performed for the sake of popularity or vanity is unstable and transitory [17.18].
verse_text: That austerity which is undertaken for earning a name, being honoured and worshipped, and also ostentatiously,-that is spoken of as born of rajas, belonging to this world, uncertain and transitory.

sentence: Krishna states that the path of right action is superior to the renunciation of action [5.2].
verse_text: The Blessed Lord said Both renunciation of actions and Karma-yoga lead to Liberation. Between the two, Karma-yoga, however, excels over renunciation of actions.

sentence: Krishna says that those who keep their minds fixed on Him, worshipping Him always with unwavering faith and concentration, are considered the best in Yoga [12.2].
verse_text: The Blessed Lord said Those who meditate on Me by fixing their minds on Me with steadfast devotion (and) being endowed with supreme faith-they are considered to be the most perfect yogis according to Me.

sentence: Krishna explains that for those who worship Him alone, thinking of no other and remaining ever-united, He secures what is not already possessed and preserves what they already possess [9.22].
verse_text: Those persons who, becoming non-different from Me and meditative, worship Me everywhere, for them, who are ever attached (to Me), I arrange for securing what they lack and preserving what they have.

sentence: Krishna also states that he who is full of faith and has his inner self merged in Him is deemed the most devout among all Yogis [6.47].
verse_text: Even among all the yogis, he who adores Me with his mind fixed on Me and with faith,he is considered by Me to be the best of the yogis.

sentence: Arjuna admits that Krishna's language perplexes him and confuses his reason, and he asks for the one way to secure his welfare [3.2].
verse_text: You bewilder my understanding, as it were, by a seemingly conflicting statement! Tell me for certain one of these by which I may attain the highest Good.

sentence: Krishna says that even the wise are confused about what is action and what is inaction [4.16].
verse_text: Even the intelligent are confounded as to what is action and what is inaction. I shall tell you of that action by knowing which you will become free from evil.

sentence: Krishna explains that knowledge, the act, and the doer differ according to the qualities [18.19].
verse_text: Knowledge, action and agent are stated in the teaching about the gunas to be only of three kinds according to the differences of the gunas. Hear about them also as they are.

sentence: Krishna says that only the unenlightened speak of wisdom and right action as separate, and he who perceives that the two are one knows the truth [5.5].
verse_text: The State [Sthana (State) is used in the derivative sense of 'the place in which one remains established, and from which one does not become relegated'.] that is reached by the Sankhyas, that is reached by the yogis as well. He sees who sees Sankhya and yoga as one.

sentence: Krishna says that the Self is unmanifested, unthinkable, and unchangeable, and that knowing this leaves no cause for grief [2.25].
verse_text: It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

sentence: Krishna explains that constant yearning for the knowledge of the Self and pondering the lessons of truth is wisdom, while everything else is ignorance [13.12].
verse_text: Steadfastness in the knowledge of the Self, contemplation on the Goal of the knowledge of Reality-this is spoken of as Knowledge. Ignorance is that which is other than this.

sentence: Krishna further states that one should know that all modifications and qualities are born of Nature [13.20].
verse_text: Know both Nature and also the individual soul [Prakrti is sometimes translated as matter, and purusa as spirit.-Tr.] to be verily without beginning; know the modifications as also the alities as born of Nature.

sentence: Krishna says that men are deluded because their wisdom is submerged in ignorance [5.15].
verse_text: The Omnipresent neither accepts anybody's sin nor even virtue. Knowledge remains covered by ignorance. Thery the creatures become deluded.

sentence: Krishna explains that from anger comes delusion, which leads to the destruction of discrimination [2.63].
verse_text: From anger follows delusion; from delusion, failure of memory; from failure of memory, the loss of understanding; from the loss of understanding, he perishes.

sentence: Krishna notes that even the wise are confused about the nature of action and inaction [4.16].
verse_text: Even the intelligent are confounded as to what is action and what is inaction. I shall tell you of that action by knowing which you will become free from evil.

sentence: Krishna states that those who do not understand the qualities of nature are attached to the functions of those qualities [3.29].
verse_text: Those who are wholly deluded by the gunas of Nature become attached to the activities of the gunas. The knower of the All should not disturb those of dull intellect, who do not know the All.

sentence: Krishna says that serenity of mind, kindness, silence, self-control, and purity constitute the austerity of the mind [17.16].
verse_text: Tranillity of mind, gentleness, reticence, withdrawal of the mind, purity of heart,-these are what is called mental austerity.

sentence: Krishna explains that one has the right to work, but never to the fruits of that work [2.47].
verse_text: Your right is for action alone, never for the results. Do not become the agent of the results of action. May you not have any inclination for inaction.

sentence: Krishna advises that one should perform actions while remaining balanced in both success and failure [2.48].
verse_text: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

sentence: Krishna states that by keeping the mind controlled and balanced, one attains a deep sense of peace [6.15].
verse_text: Concentrating the mind thus for ever, the yogi of controlled mind achieves the Peace which culminates in Liberation and which abides in Me.

sentence: Krishna says that one should perform actions while remaining balanced in both success and failure, noting that this evenness of mind is called Yoga [2.48].
verse_text: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

sentence: Krishna explains that mental austerity consists of serenity of mind, kindness, silence, self-control, and purity [17.16].
verse_text: Tranillity of mind, gentleness, reticence, withdrawal of the mind, purity of heart,-these are what is called mental austerity.

sentence: Krishna further states that a person whose senses are under control and who remains steadfast in meditation achieves steady wisdom [2.61].
verse_text: Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.

sentence: Krishna says that one should not yield to the love and hate aroused by the objects of sense, as they are foes that obstruct the path [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: Krishna explains that a person who is endowed with a pure intellect and controls the self by firmness abandons attraction and hatred [18.51].
verse_text: Being endowed with a pure intellect, and controlling oneself with fortitude, rejecting the objects-beginning from sound [Sound, touch, form and colour, taste and smell.-Tr.], and eliminating attachment and hatred;

sentence: Krishna suggests that by the help of reason controlled by fortitude, one may little by little attain peace [6.25].
verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: Krishna states that the wisdom of one who restrains the senses and remains steadfast is steady [2.61].
verse_text: Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.

sentence: Krishna says that one should look upon pleasure and pain, victory and defeat, with an equal eye [2.38].
verse_text: Treating happiness and sorrow, gain and loss, and conest and defeat with eanimity, then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.

sentence: Krishna explains that one should be endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self by firmness, and abandoning attraction and hatred [18.51].
verse_text: Being endowed with a pure intellect, and controlling oneself with fortitude, rejecting the objects-beginning from sound [Sound, touch, form and colour, taste and smell.-Tr.], and eliminating attachment and hatred;

sentence: Krishna describes qualities such as harmlessness, truth, absence of anger, and compassion towards beings [16.2].
verse_text: Non-injury, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, control of the internal organ, absence of vilification, kindness to creatures, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, freedom from restlessness;

sentence: Krishna suggests that one should surrender actions, be free from egoism, and act with a mind devoid of excitement [3.30].
verse_text: Devoid of the fever of the soul, engage in battle by dedicating all actions to Me, with (your) mind intent on the Self, and becoming free from expectations and egoism.

sentence: Krishna says that attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses, and he advises that one should not come under their sway because they are foes [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: Krishna explains that when a man dwells on objects of sense, he creates an attraction for them, which develops into desire and breeds anger [2.62].
verse_text: -2.63 In the case of a person who dwells on objects, there arises attachment for them. From attachment grows hankering, from hankering springs anger.

sentence: Krishna describes a person who is equal to friends and enemies and remains steady in situations of happiness and distress [12.18].
Krishna states that to him who has conquered his lower nature, the Self is a friend, but to him who has not done so, it acts like an enemy [6.6].
verse_text: Of him, by whom has been conered his very self by the self, his self is the friend of his self. But, for one who has not conered his self, his self itself acts inimically like an enemy.

sentence: Krishna says that one should perform actions while being steadfast in Yoga, abandoning attachment and remaining balanced in success and failure [2.48].
verse_text: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

sentence: Krishna explains that actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards [18.6].
verse_text: But even these actions have to be undertaken by renouncing attachment and (hankering for) results. This is My firm and best conclusion, O Parhta.

sentence: Krishna also describes the state of non-attachment as the non-identification of the self with son, wife, home, and the rest, along with constant even-mindedness [13.10].
verse_text: Non-attachment and absence of fondness with regard to sons, wives, homes, etc., and constant eanimity of the mind with regard to the attainment of the desirable and the undesirable;
